note: P4371 (Pro 30:18) — three things are too wonderful for me; four I do not understand.

dims.v: reverent wonder — things too wonderful to grasp

the wonder Agur feels at things too wonderful for him — the reverent amazement before mysteries that exceed his grasp (the eagle's flight, the ship's course, the way of a man with a maid), humility that marvels rather than presumes
the acknowledged ignorance it goes with (267146)
welded to the not-understanding Agur openly confesses

pala (be wonderful/beyond) — 'three things are too WONDERFUL for me' (30:18); the wise heart marvels at what it cannot fully grasp. Wonder before mystery is a mark of humility, not ignorance ashamed (cf 30:2-4).
owned mystery — Agur confessing four things he cannot understand
the not-understanding that Agur confesses of the four wonderful things — the honest owning of mystery, refusing to pretend a comprehension he lacks, wonder joined to humble ignorance
welded to the reverent amazement Agur feels
yada (know/understand), negated — 'four I do not UNDERSTAND' (30:18); Agur openly owns what he cannot comprehend. To confess the limits of one's understanding is wisdom, not failure (cf 30:2-3).
